subject: Urgent: 99th pct latency spike + token queueing impacting NimbusPay reserved capacity
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@nimbuspay.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Sudden latency + errors on reserved endpoints — impact to payments flow

Karthik,

We're seeing a sharp rise in 99th percentile latency on the Redwood dedicated endpoints we reserve for NimbusPay. Starting ~14:45 ET today our production payment authorization path experienced token queueing that resulted in elevated 500s and timeouts; a handful of authorizations were retried by downstream services which amplified load.

High level:
- Error rate: 0.9% -> 3.7% between 14:45-15:10
- 99th pct latency: ~220ms -> ~1.8s
- Throughput observed by Nimbus: nominal, no traffic spike on our side (request rate stable)

This is customer-facing and causing a few merchants to route to fallback. Can Redwood confirm whether dedicated pool saturation or reserved throughput throttling is the root cause? We have a renewal conversation next week; this needs immediate attention.

Attaching a short trace from our service showing queued tokens and request timing.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Payments - NimbusPay
[Attachment: nimbus-request-trace-20270512.log (text/plain)]

2) Marissa — let's prepare a short customer note with visibility and the short-term mitigation we can offer (burst capacity + credit proposal).
3) Samir/Elena — we'll follow up with a timeline within 30 minutes for triage and a 1-hour bridge if needed.

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Sudden latency + errors on reserved endpoints — impact to payments flow

On Wed, May 12, 2027 at 15:18, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Priyom — can you confirm GPU pool utilization and any throttling/fallbacks for NimbusPay's reserved allocation (D-98721-NIM)?

Summary of initial findings (14:30-15:10 ET window):
- Reserved pool: 8xA100-nv nodes dedicated to NimbusPay. Observed utilization spike to 96-99% across the pool at 14:42.
- Autoscaling: configured to add ephemeral burst nodes, but burst policy did not trigger because request size distribution flagged many long-context generation requests and the kernel selection stayed pinned to an older quantized path. In short, scheduler decisions prevented burst attachment.
- Token queueing: KV cache hit ratio dropped (from 87% -> 51%) as the model cache warmed/evicted; this increased per-request seq length and memory pressure leading to slower throughputs and downstream request queuing.
- Error surface: a small subset of RTT outliers caused internal timeouts; we saw internal retry loops escalate to 5xx at the API layer.

Attachments: perf-snapshot-20270512.png and token-queueing-trace-20270512.log.

Immediate mitigations applied (by infra team):
- Manually raised per-customer headroom cap by 20% to reduce queueing on reserved pool.
- Forced scheduler to favor newer quantized kernel for these models to reduce memory pressure (roll-forward patch applied at 15:33).
- Throttled non-critical background workloads that were co-located (replicated telemetry batch jobs).

Observed improvement: 99th pct down from ~1.8s to ~420ms after measures; error rates trending down but still above baseline.

Next steps:
- Ops will continue to monitor for 30m.
- Need executive approval for emergency 2-hour burst capacity (3x nodes) to restore headroom to normal SLA margins while we root-cause the autoscaler policy mismatch.
- Post-incident action item: scheduler policy review and a reserved-capacity compatibility test for quantized kernels.

Priyom Das
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: perf-snapshot-20270512.png (image/png)]

Subject: Executive alert — NimbusPay reserved pool headroom breach; recommend immediate burst and SLA exception

Team — FYI and urgent ask: NimbusPay (D-98721-NIM) experienced sustained headroom loss that led to elevated latency and a rise in 5xx errors for customer traffic between 14:40-15:10 ET. Priyom's initial remediation recovered most of the impact but we are not yet back to baseline.

Recommendation for exec approval:
- Approve emergency reserve burst: provision 3 additional A100 nodes for 2 hours (cost impact noted in CC).
- Approve temporary SLA flexibility for the renewal team to take time to run the scheduler/quantization compatibility fixes as a follow-up.
- Authorize a goodwill credit for NimbusPay covering the impacted window (Marissa to propose tiered options).

Business impact: this is a priority account in renewal cadence; prolonged degradation risks churn and escalation to their CIO. We should act fast and communicate clearly.

Please flag approvals or concerns on this thread ASAP. If approved, Operations will fire the burst and Sales will finalize the customer note.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success & Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
